name: Ke Gong
roles: BSc. in Computer Science, Dalian University of Technology
Incoming Graduate Student, UC Santa Barbara
about: I am a recent Computer Science graduate from Dalian University of Technology and an incoming graduate student at UC Santa Barbara. My work sits at the intersection of natural language processing and automatic speech recognition — I enjoy building systems that help machines understand human language in real, sometimes messy, settings.
news: I am currently in Santa Barbara and actively looking for research opportunities (RA positions).

research.title: Speech Transcription for the Sichuan–Chongqing Dialect
paragraphs: I designed a high-accuracy speech transcription system using Paraformer-large as the base model, built on a ~29,000-utterance subset of the KeSpeech dataset. To handle limited dialect data, I proposed a partial-parameter-freezing fine-tuning strategy that freezes low-level acoustic modules and fine-tunes only high-level semantic layers.

This reduced the character error rate from 9.5% to 7.05% on KeSpeech, and from 18.2% to 7.6% on the cross-corpus WSC-Eval set. Adding Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct as a post-correction module further lowered CER to 6.47%, and I deployed an interactive demo with FastAPI and Gradio that runs with a real-time factor below 0.02 on an RTX 4090.

research.title: Real-Time Detection of Illegal Content in Livestreams
paragraphs: I led the development of a system that combines speech-to-text transcription with a BERT-based classification model to detect illegal behaviors such as false advertising and exaggerated claims in e-commerce livestreams.
To address scarce training data, I tested multiple data augmentation strategies and applied domain-specific fine-tuning to improve both accuracy and robustness.

research.title: Vision-Guided Robotic Box-Handling
paragraphs: I contributed to a computer-vision-based robotic system for object recognition and automated box-handling on an Atlas development board, and developed the communication module that connects the vision-recognition module with the robot controller.

aims.title: Safer Online Information

aims.title: Language and Machines
aims.text: Exploring how perception and language help machines interact with the physical world.

life_title: From Chemical Engineering to Computer Science
life_text: I started university in chemical engineering. As I took more programming and language-related courses, I found myself increasingly drawn to how machines understand and generate human language, so I switched to computer science. That decision has shaped the work I do today.
